editorial.tldr: This thread groups ten items that share overlapping title words, not one developing story. It opened Aug 24-25 with three general-purpose anomaly-detection papers, then Aug 27-Sep 10 added a clinical-assistant comparison, two hallucination-detection papers, an agent-swarm benchmark, an HVAC deployment review, and a vendor business-model roundup -- none connected beyond the words 'detection' or 'large language models.'
editorial.whats_new: The newest addition isn't a new event -- it's three unrelated anomaly-detection papers (relational databases, industrial control systems, streaming video) from Aug 24-25 that joined this page purely because they share the word 'detection' with the hallucination-detection paper already here, and none of the three mention LLMs at all.
editorial.why_it_matters: None of these ten items report on the same product, model, or event -- treat this page as a keyword collision, not a thread whose story to follow.
editorial.take_for_builders: Don't treat a shared link on this page as corroboration across sources -- these items are grouped by word overlap only; verify each independently before citing them together.

open_questions: Does PoP's detection rate hold against sampling-based baselines such as semantic entropy, and at what accuracy cost?
Do PoP's inter-layer activation features transfer across model families, or must a detector be trained per model?
Does activation-level detection need weights access, ruling it out for API-only deployments?
Does SwarmBench report results for today's popular agent frameworks, or only for research prototypes?
Does the DeBERTa-v3 domain-specific hallucination detector generalize across domains, or need per-domain fine-tuning?
Do the three anomaly-detection papers (RAD, ICS robustness, streaming video) touch LLM-based systems anywhere, or is 'detection' purely a coincidental shared word?
